newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs follow Wall St to end up, ignore CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs follow Wall St to end up, ignore CVRD.

text.p: Brazilian stocks shrugged off delays in privatizing state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce and mimicked Wall Street's rise to end higher in strong trade in major local blue chips, brokers said.
"It was basically New York today," said John Carioba of Indusval brokerage.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa .BVSP index of 49 most-traded shares rose 1.26 percent to end at 9,982 points on healthy volume of 592.4 million reais ($557 million).
Brokers said trade rose following dividend announcements by two major blue chips, bellwether Telebras and power holding Eletrobras.

Telebras announced a payout of 1.878 reais per 1,000 shares while Eletrobras said it would pay 9.61 reais and 20.62 reais per 1,000 shares to holders of its common and preferred shares respectively, traders said.
Telebras preferred ended virtually flat at 121.99 reais while its common closed off 0.17 percent at 114.50 reais.
Eletrobras preferred B fell 1.98 percent to end at 496 reais while its common was off 0.62 percent at 481 reais.
But dealers said the broader Brazilian market, following rising New York prices, moved higher led by other power stocks and common shares of state oil company Petrobras.
Sao Paulo state power firm Cia Paulista de Forca e Luz rose 1.86 percent to end at 165.02 reais, while Petrobras common surged 4.91 percent to end at 171.00 reais.
Minas Gerais state power firm Cemig also posted gains, its preferred rising 1.04 percent to 48.49 reais.
Overall, the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE rose 0.65 percent to end at 2,718 points.
CVRD's preferred ended 0.37 percent higher to close at 27.10 reais, while its common slipped 0.31 percent to 29.40 reais.
